proof.criterion: Review finding 1 (High) - an edit that drops an option a person typed in the browser is applied, because the editor's own mark is nothing the markdown writes
proof.surface: the real dispatch CLI against a Dispatch server the tester built and started from this head (packages/dispatch/e2e/run-server.sh, port 8791, Postgres 17 with pgvector, database dispatch_tester2), issue T2-1
proof.command: dispatch comment --issue T2-1 --artifact spec.md --quote 'Matches what the platform team runs today' --body '...' (which leaves an anchor mark on that option's line, the class of mark the browser writes on every typed character); then dispatch edit-ask --ask be964a59-a1c7-4c3a-983e-95f2340515a0 --option 'gRPC: Adds streaming and server push'; then dispatch doc-read --issue T2-1 --artifact spec.md
proof.observed: The drop was accepted ('Ask edited: Which transport should we expose for the 4.2 release?') and the document holds the gRPC item whole with the REST item gone. The comment itself survives the loss of its anchor: GET /api/v1/issues/T2-5/comments shows anchor.orphaned true with its quote kept, so no comment is deleted by an edit of the text it pointed at.
proof.negativeControl: The same two commands against the implementer's build of the reviewed head 57c0bbe3 (port 8780, issue PREV-2): refused 'options: the edit drops the option "REST", whose list item holds more than its plain line ... its item reads "- REST: Matches the platform the team already runs"' - the refusal quotes a line that reads plain, which is the finding. The refusal of real content is not lost with it: on this head dispatch edit-ask --clear-options on the same ask is still refused, quoting the gRPC item's paragraph and sub-list.

proof.criterion: Review finding 3 (Medium) - a rewrite that would delete the markup in an option's own line is refused, and the step the refusal names applies
proof.surface: the same server at port 8791, issues T2-1 and T2-6
proof.command: dispatch edit-ask --ask be964a59-... --option 'REST: ...' --option 'gRPC: Adds streaming and server push' (on an item whose line reads 'gRPC: **Adds** streaming, see [the note](https://example.com/grpc)'); then the step it names, dispatch doc-edit --ops-json '[{"op":"replace","find":"**Adds** streaming, see [the note](https://example.com/grpc)","with":"Adds streaming and server push"}]'; then the same ask edit again
proof.observed: Refused: 'options: the edit rewrites the line of the option "gRPC", which holds more than its plain text, and the ask-edit route does not delete the markup a person wrote in a line; its line reads "gRPC: **Adds** streaming, see [the note](https://example.com/grpc)"; send that option back unchanged with this edit, or rewrite the line with a document edit (dispatch doc-edit, replacing quoted text with replace)', and the document was unchanged. The named document edit is accepted, leaves the second paragraph and the sub-list under the line, and the ask edit after it is accepted - so the refusal names a path an agent can take. On T2-6, whose option line holds bold and a link with nothing under it, both refusals fire with their own wording, and the drop refusal's own step (dispatch doc-edit deleting the line's block by id) removes the item cleanly and the drop is then accepted.
proof.negativeControl: The same rewrite on the reviewed head 57c0bbe3 (issue PREV-2) was accepted and the document then read '- gRPC: Adds streaming and server push': the bold and the link's address deleted with no refusal, which is the finding. A line of plain text holding markdown characters is still rewritten on this head (T2-5, 'Stars: a_b\*c and [x] and 1. not a list' reworded), so the refusal reads markup and not escaping.

observations: Round 2 answers every finding of review.json that changes behaviour, each proven at the real surface or, for finding 2, on the route: finding 1 (the editor's mark), finding 3 (the rewrite refusal), finding 4 (pairing on the whole option) and finding 2 (the row of a block holding a second list). The reviewed head reproduces findings 1, 3 and 4 under the same commands, so the fixes are read against the defect and not only against a test.

The rewrite refusal is a new refusal of work that was accepted before: an agent that rewords an option whose line a person formatted is now told to use dispatch doc-edit first. The tester followed that path end to end (replace, then the ask edit) and it applies.

A comment anchored in an option's line dies with that line when the option is dropped or its line rewritten: the comment row survives with anchor.orphaned true and its quote kept. That is the behaviour of any document edit that removes the text an anchor is on.

The tester's rigs: Postgres on 5433 (the implementer's, left running), the tester's server on 8791 (database dispatch_tester2), the implementer's builds on 8779 (this head) and 8780 (the reviewed head 57c0bbe3), test database dispatch_test_t2. Everything lives on the issue volume and goes with the pod.
